sources.correlation_scope: coverage area, route and flight length
sources.range: exact conditional retention plus declared failure-mask stress shifts of ±0.184, ±0.369 and ±0.737 percentage points; the stress shifts are not bounds
sources.evidence: release manifest; pipeline/track_quality.py; lab/uncertainty.py selection, selection-stress, selection-sensitivity and targeted-validation; selection-validation-design.json; opensky-day-audit-design.json and opensky-day-audit-result.json; selection-sensitivity-design.json; targeted-validation-design.json and targeted-validation-registration.json
sources.propagation: exact aggregate attrition; nested internal stress; one-day separate-source mask contrasts propagated at half, one and twice magnitude with first-pass CO2 exposure weights; provider-neutral 2,279-flight held-out tranche for separate mask contrasts; full independent-proxy estimator remains blocked until complete suitable external outcomes exist
sources.notes: The denominator begins after complete-flight reconstruction and successful modelling. Retention and the within-gate quality gradient are measured, and a 5,000-flight weighted validation sample is frozen outside git. A free OpenSky day shows differential match/quality response and a 4.61-point proxy offset on controls, so its conditional contrasts cannot correct or bound the headline. The central signed mask transfer is -0.014 points only because 96.3% of gross contributions cancel; coverage-only and unresolved-endpoint masks supply 94.4% of the central adverse magnitude. A separate 2,279-flight blinded tranche now targets those masks without altering the canonical design, but it remains conditional on source response and cannot cover rare masks or upstream ingestion. Changing a gate changes the target population and must be reported separately from model uncertainty.

sources.notes: New days retain internally closed aggregate counts without identifiers. The frozen release predates the funnel, so its upstream selection must remain an explicit unmeasured boundary.
